summary:
Katsina State stands under the national framework of Nigeria and additionally operates its own Shari'a criminal layer. Human Rights Watch (2004) records the spread of Shari'a adoption across northern Nigeria, listing twelve states concerned: Bauchi, Borno, Gombe, Jigawa, Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Kebbi, Niger, Sokoto, Yobe and Zamfara. The process traces from Zamfara's Shari'a Establishment Law, promulgated 27 October 1999 and in force 27 January 2000, and the provisions cited remain in force.

Katsina's own statute is the Sharia Penal Code Law 2001, Law No. 2 of 2001, which came into operation on 20 June 2001 and was gazetted in Katsina State Gazette Vol. 12 No. 23 of 27 August 2001, as annotated in Ostien's volume on Shari'a implementation in northern Nigeria.

The penalty exposure for a trans visitor in Katsina is the most severe tier documented anywhere in Nigeria. Ostien's annotation records Katsina among the three states, with Kaduna and Kebbi, whose sodomy text reads that whoever commits the offence of sodomy shall be punished with stoning to death (rajm). The same annotation's footnote 183 shows that only Kano and Katsina reach stoning to death as the maximum for the lesbianism offence, against the harmonised code's base of 50 lashes and up to six months. Katsina is therefore one of only two states whose law carries death as the maximum for same-sex acts between women as well as between men.

Wikipedia's coverage of LGBTQ rights in Nigeria describes the punishment structure across the Shari'a-governed northern states as ranging from lashing or caning to capital punishment, and records lesbianism, meaning carnal acts or stimulation between women, as punishable by imprisonment or caning in most states with death penalties applied in Kano and Katsina.

The UK Home Office country policy and information note on Nigeria, version 4.0 of June 2025, records that Nigeria operates a hybrid legal system in which a Shari'a criminal layer applies in twelve northern states, that this layer's provisions extend to women, and that arrest data for the offences is limited.
tangentialFactors:
The cross-dressing offence layer documented in the region is evidenced by a neighbouring state's court rather than by Katsina's own statute: Wikipedia records that men who dress or behave as women face prison or a fine, citing a 20 June 2025 Kano court sentence of a TikToker to one year in prison over a cross-dressing video. No equivalent Katsina prosecution or Katsina cross-dressing provision appears in the sources assembled here.

Katsina's stoning maximum for the lesbianism offence is an outlier even within the twelve Shari'a states: the harmonised northern code sets 50 lashes and up to six months, and only Kano shares Katsina's death maximum for women. For sodomy, Kaduna and Kebbi share Katsina's rajm text.
localsOnly:
Katsina residents live under the Sharia Penal Code Law 2001 as a matter of state law, in force since 20 June 2001, with sodomy carrying stoning to death and same-sex acts between women carrying a death maximum. The UK Home Office notes that the Shari'a criminal layer's provisions extend to women, so the exposure is not limited to men.

Arrest data for these offences in Katsina is limited, per the UK Home Office note of June 2025, so the frequency of local enforcement cannot be established from the sources held here.
outOfScopeNotes:
Prison placement for a trans person held in Katsina is unresolved in the sources. Wikipedia's article on LGBTQ people in prison, scanned in full, returns zero mentions of Nigeria or Nigerians, so its placement-by-gender-identity norms documented elsewhere have no Nigeria entry. The Katsina-specific article likewise carries no housing rule, no segregation or women's-wing policy and no prison-administration measure for the state.

No Katsina-specific incident of violence against a trans person, no Katsina-specific arrest figure and no Katsina-specific cross-dressing prosecution is documented in the inventory; the cross-dressing sentence cited in the sources was imposed in Kano.
